subject: BrightCart evaluation — deployment path clarification & hosted quickstart
messages: From: Jasmine Liu To: Samir Shah , Priya Desai Cc: Avery Johnson , Neha Kapoor , Aditya Rao Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 13:14:00 +0000 Subject: BrightCart evaluation — deployment path clarification & hosted quickstart Hi Samir / Priya — Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — great to see the BrightCart use case (catalog search + personalized snippets). Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and get you into a short hosted quickstart if that’s the preferred path. Recap from the call: - Primary workload: catalog search + inline product copy generation; average prompt size ~160 tokens, typical response 60–120 tokens. - Expected pilot traffic: spikes up to ~1,200 requests/min for 10–15 min; sustained baseline currently unknown. - Latency target: p95 <= 300ms for search path is desirable. - Data needs: EU residency for customer-facing data; SOC 2 evidence is required for procurement. Questions for you (short answers welcome): 1) For the pilot, do you need a VPC-only environment or can we start with Hosted API (Redwood-hosted) with EU-region tenancy? 2) Is the 1,200 req/min number a sustained expectation or burst for marketing/promotional events? 3) Any contractual constraints around data retention or logging (e.g., strict 30-day retention, no logs outside EU)? Suggested next steps if Hosted API is OK for pilot: - We provision an EU-hosted quickstart project (you get API keys and a test endpoint). - Default rate limits: 600 req/min per API key in Hosted demo tier; we can request temporary increase to 1,500 req/min for a two-week pilot after a short traffic test. - We’ll provide a short quickstart doc and an SDK snippet to wire up your search path; Neha will own the test plan. I’ve attached a one-page SOC2 summary and a short quickstart draft for your review. If Hosted shows it can meet latency and throughput during the pilot, we can keep that route. If you need guaranteed sustained throughput or private networking, Dedicated or Private VPC would be the recommendation (we’ll include sizing guidance). Can you reply with answers to the three quick questions above and suggest 30 minutes early next week for a follow-up? Thanks — Jasmine Jasmine Liu Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference [Attachment: SOC2_summary.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)] [Attachment: redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf (PDF, 0.9MB)] From: Samir Shah To: Jasmine Liu Cc: Priya Desai Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 15:03:12 +0000 Subject: Re: BrightCart evaluation — deployment path clarification & hosted quickstart Jasmine — Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers below: 1) For the pilot we prefer to start with Hosted in the EU region if it can meet the latency and throughput. We want to avoid an immediate on-prem or VPC project unless absolutely necessary. 2) The 1,200 req/min is mostly a burst requirement tied to flash promotions; baseline during normal traffic is closer to 150–200 req/min. We do sometimes see sustained 400–600 in peak shopping hours. 3) Data retention: we need to retain search telemetry for 90 days for analytics, but product PII is handled separately and must remain in our systems. SOC2 evidence is required for procurement. Main procurement concern is: if Hosted fails to meet p95 < 300ms during the pilot, we need a clear path to Dedicated with a rough estimate of cost/lead time. Also curious how Redwood handles KMS/keys for Hosted EU tenants. We can do Tuesday 09:00–09:30 UTC for a quick follow-up. Priya will join on procurement specifics. —Samir Samir Shah Head of Platform, BrightCart From: Avery Johnson To: Samir Shah , Priya Desai Cc: Jasmine Liu , Neha Kapoor , Aditya Rao Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:20:00 +0000 Subject: Re: BrightCart evaluation — deployment path clarification & hosted quickstart Samir / Priya — thanks for the quick answers, super helpful. A few tactical notes to clarify how Hosted would handle this and what triggers Dedicated: - Throughput: Hosted in our EU region can be configured to handle 1,200 req/min as a temporary increase for trials. That's typically implemented via a combination of autoscaling and a temporary quota lift; for predictable sustained load (e.g., >800 req/min baseline for multiple days) we recommend Dedicated capacity to guarantee throughput and cost predictability. - Latency: p95 <= 300ms is achievable for your prompt sizes on our optimized search model family if you use our streaming endpoints and enable prefix/KV caching for catalog embeddings. We’ll run an A/B traffic test during the pilot to validate this. - Key management: Hosted EU tenants can integrate with customer-managed KMS (Bring Your Key) for encryption at rest; for pilot we can use Redwood-managed keys, and we will surface KMS options when you move to Dedicated or Private. - Data retention: We can scope log retention per project; if you need 90-day telemetry retention scoped to EU region, that’s doable and we’ll document it in the MAP. Operational next steps I suggest: 1) Jasmine will provision an EU-hosted quickstart project and create two API keys (one for baseline test, one for burst test). 2) Neha will lead a 2-hour traffic test (synthetic pattern to replicate spikes) and capture p50/p95 at the endpoint. 3) If p95 exceeds 300ms consistently, we’ll provide a Dedicated sizing estimate and lead time (~3–4 weeks typical) and a cost delta for committed capacity. I’ll prep the temporary rate increase request and include a short checklist for the traffic test. Best, Avery Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference From: Neha Kapoor To: Samir Shah , Priya Desai Cc: Jasmine Liu , Avery Johnson , Aditya Rao Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 11:30:00 +0000 Subject: Re: BrightCart evaluation — deployment path clarification & hosted quickstart Hi Samir / Priya — looping in the quickstart artifacts and a proposed test plan. Attached: redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf (step-by-step), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (pilot milestones). Proposed 2-step pilot test (we can adapt to your infra): - Step 0: Onboard (Day 0) — I’ll share a test API key and temporary project in EU. Quick sanity tests for correctness. - Step 1: Baseline run (Day 1) — 200 req/min steady for 2 hours to validate correctness and p50/p95. - Step 2: Burst simulation (Day 2) — ramp to 1,200 req/min over 60s, hold for 10–15 minutes, then step down. Capture p50/p95 and token costs. What I’ll need from BrightCart before we start: - A test account to send traffic from (IP ranges if you need whitelisting). - Confirmation you want the temporary rate increase to 1,500 req/min during the burst test. Links & next steps: - HubSpot record: HS-987654321 (I added the MAP and procurement notes). - DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/BRG-4521-PSA (I uploaded an NDA + pilot PSA draft for review). Attachment stubs: [Attachment: redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf], [Attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx] I’ll schedule the test window once we confirm the time and IPs. If everything looks good we’ll include Dedicated sizing options in the follow-up proposal. Thanks, Neha Kapoor Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference From: Samir Shah To: Jasmine Liu , Neha Kapoor , Avery Johnson Cc: Priya Desai Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 16:05:00 +0000 Subject: Re: BrightCart evaluation — deployment path clarification & hosted quickstart Team — Thanks — this all looks great and actionable. We confirm: start with Hosted EU for the pilot, please provision the test project and issue keys. We want the temporary rate increase to 1,500 req/min for the burst simulation. I booked the Tuesday 09:00–09:30 UTC slot for the follow-up — can we make that a working session to kick off onboarding and sync on IPs/whitelisting? Priya will lead procurement review and we’ll sign the NDA/PSA once legal gives the go-ahead. Samir
